svg.text: Two Ways to Watch a Network — Signatures vs. Behaviour
the same traffic feeds both; one matches known-bad, the other records everything for hunting
network traffic (via a SPAN/tap)
Signature IDS/IPS · Snort · Suricata
rule engine matches traffic against known-bad
patterns (a rule per threat):
alert tcp any any -> $HOME_NET 445 (content:"...";)
+ catches KNOWN threats instantly, low effort
− blind to novel attacks (no rule = no alert)
− encrypted payloads defeat content rules
IDS = detect (out-of-band). IPS = block (inline):
Suricata inline can DROP; Snort is the classic IDS.
Behavioural · Zeek
protocol analysers record EVERYTHING as
structured logs (not alerts):
conn.log · dns.log · http.log · ssl.log · files.log
+ sees what signatures can't: beaconing,
rare domains, odd JA3, long connections
− no built-in "this is bad"; needs analysis
you HUNT over the logs (or feed a SIEM).
works on encrypted traffic (metadata, not content).
Known vs. unknown — you run both
Snort — the original signature IDS; huge community rule sets; the reference for "what a rule looks like".
Suricata — multi-threaded signature engine, Snort-rule compatible, PLUS protocol logging + inline IPS mode.
Zeek — not a signature tool at all; a network-traffic RECORDER for hunting and forensics.
Signatures answer "did a KNOWN threat just happen?" — fast, low-analyst-effort, but only known-bad.
Behaviour answers "what is NORMAL, and what deviates?" — catches the novel, but the work is on the analyst.
